layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Anodic behavior of 18Cr-5Ni-10Mn steels containing 0.07 to 0.35% nitrogen was studied in a 0.1N

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution with additions of 0.01 to 0.1N NaCl. The nitrogen content in these steels does not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: significantly affect their passive behavior but increases their pitting resistance. The most susceptible

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sites for pit nucleation are boundaries between the austenite matrix and some second-phase

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: precipitates (presumably carbides). The effect of nitrogen on the pitting resistance of Cr-Ni-Mn steels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is discussed with respect to their phase compositions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The chromium-manganese steels may be modified by additions of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nickel (commonly 4 to 5%) and nitrogen, which both are effective

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as austenite-stabilizing components. Since the introduction of N

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into a steel is a rather difficult technological process, this element is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: most often added together with Mn. The upper limit of the N

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: content in 18Cr steel is about 0.2%,1 but in the presence of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: about 10% Mn, it can be raised to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: without initiating

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formation of gas bubbles within the solid metal. The lower limit of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the N content necessary to stabilize the austenitic phase at a given

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cr and Ni content depends upon the presence of other elements,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: particularly carbon.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The corrosion behavior of 18Cr-5Ni steels alloyed with Mn and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: N is not well known.³ The behavior in chloride solutions is an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: important concern. No systematic investigation of the effect of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nitrogen on the susceptibility of these steels to pitting has been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performed. The aim of this work, in connection with the previous

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: work,³ was to bridge this gap.

layout_dets.text: Phase Composition

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Metallographic examination showed that in the hot-forged

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: condition the steels with 0.12, 0.25, and 0.35% N were austenitic,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: whereas those with 0.07 and 0.17% N contained austenite with a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: small amount of δ-ferrite (with an excess of Cr and relatively less

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fe, Ni, and Mn than in the γ-phase). Some small second-phase

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: particles also occurred. Electron microprobe analysis identified

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these particles as carbides

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: type) and carbonitrides

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure and composition of the precipitates in 18Cr-5Ni-10Mn

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels due to different N contents were not studied.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The X-ray analysis did not detect any σ-phase in the materials

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: under investigation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Quenching did not induce a significant change in the phase

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: composition, apart from a certain homogenization of the alloys. In

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the two-phase steels, the boundaries between δ and γ-phases became

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: less susceptible to etching; the inclusions of carbides and carbo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nitrides underwent coagulation, and their number decreased slightly.

layout_dets.text: Metallographic Examination After Corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Typical micrographs of specimens after corrosion are shown in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figures 6-8. In the as-received (hot forged) steels containing the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: δ-phase (Figure 6), the formation of pits is assisted by the attack on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the δ-phase, and the grains of both δ and γ-phases show a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the δ-phase is not attacked (Figure 7).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The explanation of differences in the corrosion behavior of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: given previously.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Microscopic examination revealed that the most susceptible

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and 8). When free of these precipitates, the grains of the austenite

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are not attacked.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Discussion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In austenitic stainless steels, the nitrogen is partly present in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solid solution, and partly occurs as precipitate particles (nitrides and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: carbonitrides). The distribution ratio depends upon the N content.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The upper limit of N concentration in solid solution is determined

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by its solubility in the austenite of the given composition.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Therefore, at higher N contents, its distribution in precipitates must

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: increase.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Consequently, it might be expected that in the steels under

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: investigation, the composition and the properties of the austenite

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: should not change very much with N content. On the contrary, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quantity of carbonitrides should increase.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It is known that alloying elements which improve the passivity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the steel (Cr, Mo) increase the pitting resistance. On the other

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hand, some nonmetallic inclusions and precipitates of second

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: phases, e.g., sulfides and complex sulfide-oxide inclusions, nucleate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It is thought that the passive film over the matrix-inclusion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: boundaries are very defective. This favors the localized attack and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decreases the stability of the passive state. However, other observa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pits. -10

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: titanium sulfide, do not initiate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions indicate that some second-phase particles and inclusions, e.g.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The present results show that the higher N contents in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 18Cr-5Ni-10Mn steel improve the pitting resistance, but do not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: practically affect its passivation tendency. Corrosion pits mainly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nucleate in the vicinity of precipitated particles.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It may be suggested that in the steels under investigation, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: austenitic phase determines their ability to passivate. The second-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: phase precipitates do not significantly affect the passive state, but

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: influence the susceptibility to pitting.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Some literature data show that in Cr-Ni-Mn-N steels the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nitrogen forms carbonitrides of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: type with a consider-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: able C content, while the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: carbides do not incorporate N.12

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: An increase of the N content in the steel can induce either: (1)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an increase of the quantitative ratio of carbonitrides to carbides, or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (2) an increase of the N content in carbonitrides.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the first case, the amelioration of the pitting resistance would

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be due to a relative reduction of the number of carbide particles

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which are assumed to nucleate pits. In the second case, it is assumed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that with enrichment of the carbonitrides in nitrogen, the corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance of their boundaries with the austenitic phase increases. At

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: present, there is no decisive evidence indicating which of the above

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two assumptions is correct. However, observations made in our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: previous study,3 namely that in 18Cr-5Ni-Mn steels with very low N

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: content the pits are predominantly nucleated at the carbide

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: particles, favors the first explanation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Conclusions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. The presence of 0.07 to 0.35% N in 18Cr-5Ni-10Mn steels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: does not affect its practical ability to promote passivation in 0.1N

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solutions containing from 0.01 to 0.1 N NaCl (the values of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ikp, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: do not change with the composition of the steel).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. The pitting resistance increases with N content

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: increases whereas number of pitsdecreases with N content).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. The most susceptible locations for pit nucleation in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 18Cr-5Ni-10Mn steels, irrespective of N content, are boundaries

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: between the austenite matrix and some precipitated particles

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (presumably carbides).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4. The beneficial effect of N can balance the detrimental effect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of Mn on the resistance of 18Cr-5Ni steels to pitting.
